docs.title: Home
docs.text:
core-backend

A modern, modular, and high-performance FastAPI boilerplate with async SQLAlchemy 2.0 and PostgreSQL.

Get Started →

docs.title: Explore the Documentation
docs.text:
🚀 Getting Started

Set up your local development environment and run your first API request.

🏗️ Architecture

Understand the modular design patterns and project structure.

Browse the available endpoints for authentication, users, and more.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 🚀 FastAPI Powered: High-performance, async-first web framework.
  • 🔐 JWT Security: Robust authentication with access & refresh tokens and token blacklisting (HS256).
  • 🗄️ Async ORM: SQLAlchemy 2.0 with asyncio support for PostgreSQL (asyncpg) and PostGIS.
  • 🛡️ Data Validation: Pydantic v2 for seamless schema validation and environment settings.
  • 📈 Structured Logging: Enhanced observability using structlog and custom middleware.
  • ⚡ Dependency Management: Managed with uv for blazing-fast installations.
  • 🐳 Dockerized: One-command development and production environments.
  • 🔄 DB Migrations: Schema versioning via Alembic.
  • 🧹 Code Quality: Linting and formatting with ruff.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/Matto-Lebars/FastAPI-Boilerplate.git && cd fastapi-boilerplate

# 2. Configure environment
cp ./docker/local_uvicorn/.env.example ./src/.env

# 3. Run local uvicorn server with Docker Compose
docker compose -f ./docker/local_uvicorn/docker-compose.yml up --build

The API will be available at http://localhost:8000. Interactive docs at http://localhost:8000/docs.

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Web Framework FastAPI ORM SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async) Database PostgreSQL + PostGIS Migrations Alembic Auth python-jose (JWT HS256) + bcrypt Validation Pydantic v2 Logging structlog + Rich Package Manager uv Containerization Docker & Docker Compose

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The project follows a modular and layered architecture to ensure maintainability, scalability, and ease of testing.

docs.title: High-Level Overview
docs.text:
graph TD
    Client(["🌐 Client"])
    Middleware["Middleware(Logging, CORS)"]
    API["API Layer app/api/v1/"]
    Deps["Dependencies (Auth, DB Session)"]
    CRUD["CRUD Layer app/crud/"]
    DB[("PostgreSQL + PostGIS")]
    Schemas["Pydantic Schemas app/schemas/"]
    Models["SQLAlchemy Models app/models/"]

    Client --> Middleware
    Middleware --> API
    API --> Deps
    API --> Schemas
    Deps --> CRUD
    CRUD --> Models
    Models --> DB

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
src/
├── alembic.ini                 # Alembic configuration
├── .env                        # Environment variables (not committed)
├── migrations/                 # Alembic migration scripts
│   └── versions/
└── app/
    ├── main.py                 # Application entry point
    ├── api/
    │   ├── dependencies.py     # Shared FastAPI dependencies (auth, db)
    │   └── v1/                 # Versioned route handlers
    │       ├── health.py
    │       ├── login.py
    │       ├── logout.py
    │       └── user.py
    ├── core/
    │   ├── config.py           # Pydantic settings (all env vars)
    │   ├── logger.py           # structlog configuration
    │   ├── setup.py            # Application factory
    │   ├── auth/               # JWT, hashing, security
    │   ├── database/           # Engine, session, base model
    │   ├── exceptions/         # Custom HTTP exceptions
    │   └── helper/             # Pagination and common utilities
    ├── crud/                   # Database CRUD operations
    ├── models/                 # SQLAlchemy ORM models
    ├── schemas/                # Pydantic request/response schemas
    └── middleware/             # Custom FastAPI middlewares

docs.title: 1. API Layer (app/api/)
docs.text:
Defines RESTful endpoints. Responsibilities:

  • Validate incoming requests using Pydantic schemas
  • Extract dependencies (current user, DB session)
  • Delegate business logic to the CRUD layer
  • Return typed responses
@router.post("/user", response_model=UserRead, status_code=201)
async def write_user(
    user: UserCreate,
    db: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)],
) -> UserRead:
    ...

docs.title: 2. Dependencies (app/api/dependencies.py)
docs.text:
FastAPI's Depends() system is used to inject common logic into routes:

Dependency Description get_db Provides an async SQLAlchemy session get_current_user Validates the Bearer token and returns the authenticated user get_current_superuser Ensures the user has superuser privileges get_optional_user Returns the user if authenticated, or None

docs.title: 3. CRUD Layer (app/crud/)
docs.text:
Encapsulates all database access logic. Uses a generic CRUDBase class that provides:

  • get(db, **filters) — fetch a single record
  • get_multi(db, offset, limit, filters) — fetch a paginated list
  • create(db, obj_in) — insert a new record
  • update(db, obj, update_data) — update a record
  • delete(db, **filters) — soft or hard delete

docs.title: 4. Models Layer (app/models/)
docs.text:
SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models. All inherit from BaseModel, which provides:

  • id — UUID primary key
  • created_at / updated_at — auto-managed timestamps
  • is_deleted — soft deletion flag

docs.title: 5. Schemas Layer (app/schemas/)
docs.text:
Pydantic v2 schemas for each resource. Typically split into:

Schema Purpose UserCreate Data the client sends to register a user UserCreateInternal Internal schema including hashed_password UserUpdate Partial update schema UserRead Data returned to the client (excludes password)

docs.title: 6. Core Layer (app/core/)
docs.text:
The central hub:

  • config.py — all configuration via pydantic-settings, loaded from .env
  • auth/ — JWT creation/verification and password hashing
  • database/ — async engine setup and session factory
  • exceptions/ — custom HTTPException subclasses (e.g. NotFoundException, ForbiddenException)
  • helper/ — pagination utilities

docs.title: Request Lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant M as Middleware
    participant R as Router (API v1)
    participant D as Dependencies
    participant CR as CRUD
    participant DB as PostgreSQL

    C->>M: HTTP Request
    M->>R: Forward (log request ID)
    R->>D: Resolve get_current_user, get_db
    D->>DB: Verify token (blacklist check)
    R->>CR: Call CRUD method
    CR->>DB: Async SQL query
    DB-->>CR: Result rows
    CR-->>R: Return domain object
    R-->>M: JSON Response
    M-->>C: HTTP Response (log status)

docs.title: Design Patterns
docs.text: Pattern Where Used Application Factory core/setup.py — creates the FastAPI app with settings Dependency Injection api/dependencies.py — database sessions and authentication Repository / CRUD crud/ — centralised, reusable database access Versioned API /api/v1/ — backward-compatible routing Async Everything asyncpg driver + AsyncSession + async def endpoints Soft Deletion is_deleted flag on models, filtered in queries

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Follow these instructions to get your development environment up and running.

docs.title: Setup Options
docs.text:
🐳 Docker🖥️ Native (Local)

Prerequisites

  • Docker & Docker Compose

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.14+
  • uv — fast Python package and project manager
  • Docker & Docker Compose — for running PostgreSQL with PostGIS (optional, but recommended for local development)
  • PostgreSQL — with PostGIS extension (optional)

docs.title: 1. Navigate to the Docker Directory
docs.text: cd docker/local_uvicorn

docs.title: 2. Build and Start All Services
docs.text:
docker compose up --build

This starts:

  • The FastAPI application with hot-reloading
  • A PostgreSQL + PostGIS database container
  • Runs Alembic migrations automatically
  • Creates the initial superuser automatically

Note

The first build may take a few minutes to pull images and install dependencies.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Matto-Lebars/FastAPI-Boilerplate.git
cd core-backend

docs.title: 2. Install Dependencies
docs.text:
uv sync

This creates a virtual environment and installs all dependencies defined in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: 3. Configure Environment
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file and edit it with your local settings:

cp docker/local_uvicorn/.env.example src/.env

Tip

Set POSTGRES_SERVER=localhost if your database is running locally (not in Docker).

Key variables to configure:

Variable Description Default POSTGRES_SERVER Database host localhost POSTGRES_USER Database username postgres POSTGRES_PASSWORD Database password postgres POSTGRES_DB Database name postgres SECRET_KEY JWT signing key (change this!) ENVIRONMENT local, staging, or production local

docs.title: 4. Start PostgreSQL in Docker (preferred) or Ensure Local DB is Running
docs.text:
If you don't have a local PostgreSQL instance, you can start one using Docker:

docker compose -f ./docker/local_uvicorn/docker-compose.yml up -d db

docs.title: 5. Run Migrations
docs.text:
Ensure your PostgreSQL instance is running, then apply all migrations:

uv run alembic -c src/alembic.ini upgrade head

docs.title: 6. Create the First Superuser
docs.text:
uv run python -m src.scripts.create_first_superuser

Default credentials are read from your .env file (ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD).

docs.title: 7. Start the Development Server
docs.text:
uv run uvicorn src.app.main:app --reload

The API is now available at http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Verifying the Setup
docs.text:
Once running, check the following URLs:

URL Description http://localhost:8000/docs Interactive Swagger UI http://localhost:8000/redoc ReDoc documentation http://localhost:8000/api/v1/health Application health check http://localhost:8000/api/v1/ready Readiness check (includes DB)

docs.title: 1. Log in to get a token
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "username=admin@admin.com&password=!Ch4ng3Th1sP4ssW0rd!"

Response: 

{
  "access_token": "eyJ...",
  "refresh_token": "eyJ...",
  "token_type": "bearer"
}

docs.title: 2. Call a protected endpoint
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8000/api/v1/user/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>"

docs.title: Embedded bruno collection
docs.text:
Prerequisites

  • bruno — API testing and documentation tool

You can also explore the API using the embedded bruno collection. To do this open the bruno app and import the folder bruno_collection in the root of the project. This collection contains pre-configured requests for all API endpoints, allowing you to test and understand the API without writing any code.

docs.title: API Reference (v1)
docs.text: This project provides a versioned API under the /api/v1/ prefix.

docs.title: 🔐 Authentication & Login
docs.text: Endpoints for user authentication and session management.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/v1/login
  • Description: Authenticate with username/email and password.
  • Payload: OAuth2PasswordRequestForm (username, password).
  • Response: Token (access_token, token_type). Sets a refresh_token in a HttpOnly cookie.

docs.title: Refresh Access Token
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/v1/refresh
  • Description: Issue a new access token using the refresh token from the cookie.
  • Payload: None (reads from cookie).
  • Response: Token (access_token, token_type).

docs.title: Logout
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/v1/logout
  • Description: Invalidate the current session by blacklisting the tokens and clearing the refresh cookie.
  • Requires Auth: Yes (Bearer Token).

docs.title: 👤 User Management
docs.text: Endpoints for managing user accounts.

docs.title: Create User
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/v1/user
  • Description: Register a new user account.
  • Requires Auth: No.
  • Payload: UserCreate (email, username, password, etc.).

docs.title: List Users
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /api/v1/users
  • Description: Fetch a paginated list of all non-deleted users.
  • Query Params: page (default 1), items_per_page (default 10).
  • Response: PaginatedListResponse[UserRead].

docs.title: Read Current User
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /api/v1/user/me
  • Description: Get details of the currently authenticated user.
  • Requires Auth: Yes (Bearer Token).

docs.title: Update User
docs.text:
• Endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/user/{username}
  • Description: Update details for the specified user.
  • Requires Auth: Yes (Bearer Token, must be owner).
  • Payload: UserUpdate (partial updates for email, username, name, etc.).

docs.title: Delete User (Soft)
docs.text:
• Endpoint: DELETE /api/v1/user/{username}
  • Description: Mark a user account as deleted and blacklist the current token.
  • Requires Auth: Yes (Bearer Token, must be owner).

docs.title: 🏥 Health Checks
docs.text: Endpoints to monitor the application's status.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /api/v1/health
  • Description: Basic check to ensure the application is running. Returns the environment and current version.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /api/v1/ready
  • Description: Comprehensive check including database connectivity. Returns 503 Service Unavailable if the database is unreachable.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This project uses pydantic-settings for centralized configuration management.

docs.title: 🛠️ Settings Architecture
docs.text: All configuration is managed in src/app/core/config.py. Settings are divided into logical base classes (e.g., AppSettings, PostgresSettings, CORSSettings) and then combined into a single Settings class.

docs.title: Key Configuration Classes
docs.text:
• AppSettings: Basic metadata about the application.
  • CryptSettings: Security, hashing, and JWT signing settings.
  • PostgresSettings: Database connection details for PostgreSQL.
  • EnvironmentSettings: Determines the environment mode (local, staging, production).
  • CORSSettings: Configures Cross-Origin Resource Sharing.
  • FirstUserSettings: Credentials for the initial superuser.

docs.title: 📄 Environment Variables
docs.text: Settings are loaded from environment variables or a .env file in the project root.

docs.title: The .env File
docs.text:
The application looks for a .env file at the root of the project (parent of src). You can copy the template: 

cp docker/local_uvicorn/.env.example src/.env

Important

Never commit your .env file to version control. It contains sensitive credentials.

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
# Database Settings
POSTGRES_USER=postgres
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=my_secure_password
POSTGRES_SERVER=db
POSTGRES_DB=app_db

# Security Settings
SECRET_KEY=generate_a_long_random_string
ENVIRONMENT=local

docs.title: ➕ Adding New Settings
docs.text:
To add a new setting:

  1. Identify the Class: Decide which base class in src/app/core/config.py your new setting belongs to.
  2. Add the Field: Add the field with a type hint and an optional default value. 
    class AppSettings(BaseSettings):
    ...
    NEW_SETTING: str = "default_value"
  3. Use the Setting: Access the setting anywhere in the app via the settings object. 
    from src.app.core.config import settings
print(settings.NEW_SETTING)

docs.title: 🧬 Dynamic Properties
docs.text:
Some settings are dynamically calculated using Pydantic's @computed_field. For example, POSTGRES_URI is automatically constructed from individual host, user, and password variables.

@computed_field
@property
def POSTGRES_URI(self) -> str:
    return f"postgresql+asyncpg://{self.POSTGRES_USER}:{self.POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@{self.POSTGRES_SERVER}/{self.POSTGRES_DB}"

docs.title: Database & Migrations
docs.text: This project uses SQLAlchemy 2.0 with asyncio and Alembic for schema management.

docs.title: 🗄️ Models Architecture
docs.text:
All database models inherit from BaseModel (located in src/app/core/database/models.py), which provides standard fields for all entities:

  • uuid: Primary key (UUIDv7, ordered and time-sorted).
  • created_at: Creation timestamp.
  • modified_at: Last modification timestamp.
  • created_by / modified_by: Foreign keys to the User who created or modified the record.
  • is_deleted / deleted_at: Soft deletion flags.

docs.title: Example Model Definition
docs.text:
from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from ..core.database.models import BaseModel

class MyEntity(BaseModel):
    __tablename__ = "my_entity"
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50), nullable=False)

docs.title: 🛠️ CRUD Operations
docs.text: We use a generic CRUDBase class in src/app/core/helper/crud.py to handle standard database operations asynchronously.

docs.title: Common CRUD Methods
docs.text:
• get(db, **lookup): Fetch one record by its unique identifiers.
  • get_multi(db, offset, limit, filters, sort_columns, sort_orders): Paginated fetch of multiple records.
  • create(db, obj_in): Create a new record from a Pydantic schema.
  • update(db, db_obj, obj_in): Update an existing record with fields from a Pydantic schema.
  • soft_delete(db, db_obj): Mark a record as deleted without removing it from the database.
  • hard_delete(db, db_obj): Permanently remove a record.
  • exists(db, **lookup): Check if a record exists matching the given criteria.

docs.title: Using CRUD in Routers
docs.text:
from src.app.crud.crud_user import crud_user

# Inside a FastAPI endpoint
user = await crud_user.get(db=db, uuid=user_uuid)

docs.title: 🔄 Migrations with Alembic
docs.text: Alembic handles database schema versioning.

docs.title: 1. Create a New Migration
docs.text:
After modifying a model in src/app/models/, generate a new migration script: 

uv run alembic -c src/alembic.ini revision --autogenerate -m "describe changes here"

docs.title: 2. Apply Migrations
docs.text:
Update your local database to the latest schema: 

uv run alembic -c src/alembic.ini upgrade head

docs.title: 3. Revert Migrations
docs.text:
Roll back the last migration: 

uv run alembic -c src/alembic.ini downgrade -1

docs.title: 🔍 Database Health Checks
docs.text: The application includes a built-in health check for the database connection: - Endpoint: /api/v1/ready - Logic: src/app/core/health.py

docs.title: Security & Authentication
docs.text: This document details the project's security implementation, focusing on JWT authentication and user authorization.

docs.title: 🔐 Authentication Mechanism
docs.text: We use JWT (JSON Web Tokens) with the HS256 algorithm for stateless authentication.

docs.title: Token Types
docs.text:
1. Access Token: Short-lived (default 30 mins) used to authenticate requests.
  2. Refresh Token: Long-lived (default 7 days) used to obtain new access tokens.

docs.title: 🍪 Token Storage & Security
docs.text:
• Access Token: Returned in the JSON response body.
  • Refresh Token: Stored in a HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie to prevent XSS attacks.

docs.title: Authentication Flow
docs.text:
1. Login: /api/v1/login returns an access_token and sets a refresh_token cookie.
  2. Requests: Client sends Authorization: Bearer <access_token> in headers.
  3. Refresh: /api/v1/refresh uses the refresh cookie to issue a new access token.
  4. Logout: /api/v1/logout blacklists both tokens and clears the refresh cookie.

docs.title: 🚫 Token Blacklisting
docs.text:
To support immediate logout and session invalidation, we use a database-backed Token Blacklist.

  • Model: TokenBlacklist (in src/app/core/auth/token_blacklist.py)
  • Action: When a token is verified, we check if it's already in the blacklist.
  • Cleanup: (TODO) Implement a background task to remove expired tokens from the blacklist.

docs.title: 🛡️ User Authorization
docs.text:
FastAPI dependencies (in src/app/api/dependencies.py) handle authorization:

  • get_current_user: Validates the access token and returns the authenticated User object.
  • get_current_superuser: Checks the is_superuser flag on the current user.
  • get_optional_user: Validates the token if present, but doesn't require it.

docs.title: 🔑 Password Hashing
docs.text:
We use bcrypt for secure password hashing.

  • Storage: Only the hashed password is ever stored in the database.
  • Comparison: bcrypt.checkpw() is used to verify passwords during login.
  • Implementation: Located in src/app/core/auth/security.py.

docs.title: 🛠️ Security Settings
docs.text:
Settings are managed in src/app/core/config.py under the CryptSettings class:

Variable Description Default SECRET_KEY Key for signing JWTs secret-key (CHANGE THIS!) ALGORITHM Hashing algorithm HS256 ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES Access token lifespan 30 REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS Refresh token lifespan 7

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text: This document outlines the standard development practices and tools used in this project.

docs.title: 🛠️ Essential Tools
docs.text:
• uv: Used for all package and project management tasks. It's significantly faster than pip and poetry.
  • ruff: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter.
  • pytest: The preferred testing framework.

docs.title: 🧹 Code Quality (Linting & Formatting)
docs.text: We use Ruff to maintain high code quality and consistent formatting. Configuration is located in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Check for Linting Errors
docs.text: uv run ruff check .

docs.title: Auto-fix Linting Errors
docs.text: uv run ruff check --fix .

docs.title: Format Code
docs.text:
uv run ruff format .

Tip

We recommend configuring your IDE (VS Code, PyCharm, etc.) to run Ruff on save.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text: While a comprehensive test suite is under development, pytest is configured as the primary testing tool.

docs.title: Run All Tests
docs.text: uv run pytest

docs.title: 🔄 Development Cycle
docs.text:
1. Create a Branch: Always work on a new feature or bugfix branch. 
    git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
  2. Local Development: Run the application locally with hot-reloading. 
    uv run uvicorn src.app.main:app --reload
  3. Verify Changes: Run linting and tests before committing. 
    uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format .
# uv run pytest (if tests are available)
  4. API Testing: Use the embedded Bruno collection or Swagger UI at http://localhost:8000/docs.
  5. Commit & Push: Follow conventional commit messages if possible. 
    git add .
git commit -m "feat: add amazing new feature"
git push origin feature/your-feature-name

docs.title: 📜 Project Scripts
docs.text:
The project includes utility scripts in src/scripts/:

  • create_first_superuser.py: Creates the initial administrator account. 
    uv run python -m src.scripts.create_first_superuser

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: This project supports containerized deployment using Docker and automated documentation publishing with GitHub Actions.

docs.title: 🐳 Dockerized Deployment
docs.text: The project is fully dockerized with a multi-stage Dockerfile optimized for size and security.

docs.title: Dockerfile Highlights
docs.text:
• Base Image: python:3.14-slim
  • Builder Stage: Uses uv to install dependencies and compile bytecode.
  • Final Stage:
    • Minimal runtime environment.
    • Runs as a non-root user (app) for security.
    • Exposes port 8000.
  • Server: Uses uvicorn (with optional gunicorn configuration for production).

docs.title: Production Build
docs.text:
To build and run the production image manually: 

docker build -t my-fastapi-app -f docker/local_uvicorn/Dockerfile .
docker run -p 8000:8000 my-fastapi-app

docs.title: 🏗️ Infrastructure with Docker Compose
docs.text:
For more complex setups, the docker-compose.yml in docker/local_uvicorn/ manages multiple services:

  1. app: The FastAPI backend.
  2. db: PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension.

docs.title: Running in Production Mode
docs.text: While the provided compose file is for local development, it can be adapted for production by: - Setting ENVIRONMENT=production in .env. - Removing --reload from the uvicorn command. - Using a persistent volume for the database.

docs.title: Documentation Publishing
docs.text:
We use GitHub Actions to automatically build and deploy this MkDocs documentation to GitHub Pages.

  • Workflow: .github/workflows/docs.yml
  • Trigger: Every push to the main branch.
  • Tools: uv handles dependency installation and mkdocs gh-deploy handles the deployment.

docs.title: API Deployment (TODO)
docs.text: Consider adding a GitHub Action workflow to: 1. Run tests and linting. 2. Build the Docker image. 3. Push the image to a container registry (Docker Hub, GHCR). 4. Deploy to your hosting provider (AWS, GCP, DigitalOcean, etc.).

docs.title: 📝 Best Practices for Production
docs.text:
1. Secrets Management: Never use the default SECRET_KEY. Use a secure vault or environment variables.
  2. Database Backups: Regularly back up your PostgreSQL volumes.
  3. HTTPS: Always serve the API behind a reverse proxy (like Nginx or Traefik) that handles SSL termination.
  4. Monitoring: Use the /api/v1/ready endpoint to configure health checks in your deployment orchestrator (Kubernetes, Docker Swarm, etc.).
